clue.text: Cheese dish (more properly a bun?)

parts.note: the toasted cheese dish from Wales was originally called after a small furry animal, and 'bun' is a pet name for that animal

explanation.surface: A pedant insists that a cheese snack should really be called a bun.
explanation.walkthrough: The dish was first called 'Welsh rabbit'; the fancier spelling came later, so 'more properly' it is a rabbit, which children call a bun or bunny.
explanation.definitionFit: Melted cheese on toast is a Welsh savoury, the dish named in the clue.

clue.text: Saskia was double Dutch to him

definitions.text: Saskia was double Dutch to him

parts.words: Saskia was double Dutch to him
parts.note: Saskia van Uylenburgh was a Dutch painter's wife, and 'old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife, so she was Dutch twice over

explanation.surface: Someone could not understand a woman called Saskia at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text reads 'Stria'; the page prints 'Saskia'. 'Double Dutch' means gibberish, but here she was Dutch and his 'Dutch', rhyming slang for wife (Duchess of Fife).
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch master of the Night Watch married Saskia, who was both Dutch and his wife.

clue.text: Musical, young Quaker?

clue.text: Such acts disqualified some — Protestants

explanation.definitionFit: A lottery-style draw disposes of items by chance, and Hornung's hero is a famous fictional burglar.

clue.text: In process of beating — using club to start game?

definitions.meaning: playing a club as the first card at bridge

clue.text: Chairman's efforts help to get it carried

explanation.surface: A committee chairman works to get a motion passed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'chairmen' were the two bearers of an old enclosed chair carried on poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat on poles borne by two porters.

clue.text: Sullen evangelist

explanation.definitionFit: Sullen is a synonym of glum, and Dwight Moody was a famous American revivalist preacher.

clue.text: Grit round a sign, showing Hassan's destination

indicators.note: the grit is placed all round, enclosing the other pieces

clue.text: Like those moving in some circles in society ?

definitions.text: Like those moving in some circles in society ?

parts.note: read socially it suggests mixing in certain social circles; literally it describes things turning in circles, and also the members of a service club

explanation.surface: A remark about the kind of people who move in particular social circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that turns round in circles is revolving, and the members of a well-known service club belong to an international society of that name.

clue.text: Support for-middle of anthers in flower

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter word anthers is taken

explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' looks like opening batsmen in cricket but is the definition: starts.

clue.text: Do this with grievance, if not patient

in a hospital, the one who is not the patient tends the sick

explanation.definitionFit: One nurses a grudge by brooding on it, and a hospital carer looks after the sick.

clue.text: No robberies in these business premises?

definitions.text: No robberies in these business premises?

parts.note: read as '...' it suggests places where money has stopped changing hands, i.e. no thefts; really they are places where trading happens

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether these trading floors are free of theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock or corn markets are trading halls, business premises where goods and shares are bought and sold.

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Routine punishment, 11

definitions.meaning: the wheel turned by prisoners' feet in Victorian jails
refers to the answer at 11 across, something that moves round in circles

clue.text: He got away with one point in three

clue.text: Silly way umpire, referee or judge reaches conclusion

definitions.text: way umpire, referee or judge reaches conclusion
definitions.meaning: each of the three officials' names ends in the same letter

clue.text: Infernal way Virgil wrote of this lake

explanation.surface: Virgil described a hellish route by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgil's line 'facilis descensus Averno' (the descent to hell is easy) names it.

clue.text: Clarifying gen — did co mix it up?

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Clarifying a coded message means working out what it says, translating the cipher.

clue.text: Judge's opinions raised at Police Department

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

clue.text: Paper dared to reset this cover twice

clue.text: Current form system

clue.text: Composer — English by' the way

explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was a leading Tudor composer of church music in England.

clue.text: Cook enjoyed it less than the majority

clue.text: Put beside sea, well away from surface
